_comment: SHARED GUARDRAIL CONFORMANCE FIXTURE — this file exists in BOTH repos and must be byte-identical.
plane: backend/app/data/guardrail_conformance.json   (tests/test_guardrail_conformance.py)
sdk:   tests/data/guardrail_conformance.json         (tests/test_guardrail_conformance.py)
Every case is `config` + `input` -> an expected outcome. Each side writes a thin adapter that
resolves the config, runs the detector and summarises, then asserts against `expect`. Agreement
stops being a matter of reading each other's prose and becomes a test run.
WHY THIS EXISTS. `pii`/`secrets` shipped on both sides from a written handover, faithfully, and
still diverged in four ways — because the contract spans TWO modules per side and only one of
them was pinned. The detectors were mirrored and tested; the config RESOLVERS were prose and
were not. `{'entities': []}` raised on the plane and PASSED in the SDK, which is a detection
control reporting success while inspecting nothing.
RULES.
1. Add a case here BEFORE changing a resolver or detector on either side.
2. Never edit one copy alone. The plane's test_detectors_mirror.py compares the two files
byte-for-byte when the SDK is present, so a one-sided edit fails there.
3. `expect.raises` means the check could NOT run: the payload is uninspected, so the caller
must surface an error and let `on_error` decide. It NEVER means 'found nothing'.
4. `expect.detail` is the exact dict recorded in guardrail_executions.result_detail (plane:
detectors.summarize_*, sdk: the runner's `metadata`). Counts, never values.
Ownership for these two types: the DETECTORS are the SDK's and the plane mirrors them; the
CONFIG RESOLVERS are the plane's and the SDK mirrors those. See docs/Guardrail_Type_Contract.md.

pii.name: absent entities scans the default four
a single entity string is accepted, not treated as characters
surrounding whitespace in an entity name is tolerated
a repeated entity is scanned once, not twice
an empty entity list is refused, never read as 'found nothing'
an unknown entity is refused rather than silently dropped
an unknown entity is refused even alongside a known one
a non-list entities value is refused
an unknown backend is refused rather than falling back to regex
a 16-digit order number is NOT a card number
ip and iban are opt-in, not scanned by default
ip and iban are detected when asked for
a clean payload passes
pii.input: Our support hours are 9 to 5, Monday to Friday.

secrets.name: an AWS key id is detected
one credential can match two patterns, and both are recorded
a private key header is detected
config is ignored — there is no detection config to get wrong

mask.name: pii: every span redacted, the rest kept
pii: a Luhn-invalid run is left alone
secrets: overlapping patterns merge into ONE redaction
a longer token does not shift later spans (right-to-left)
a mask token containing a backreference is inserted literally
nothing to mask leaves the payload untouched
